stem: A 6-year-old boy has a painless midline submental lump present for many months, and what is the most important point to explain before elective excision?

options.text: The lesion may communicate intracranially, so it should be investigated carefully before surgery
The lesion should move with tongue protrusion if it is benign
Immediate oral antibiotics are required before any further assessment
The lesion is most likely a reactive lymph node and can simply be observed
The standard operation is an intra-oral excision including the sublingual gland

explanation: The correct answer is that the lesion may communicate intracranially, so it should be investigated carefully before surgery. This is the key counselling point for a midline dermoid cyst before elective excision.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Midline dermoid cyst

optionExplanations.A: Correct because a midline dermoid cyst may have an intracranial communication, so careful assessment is needed before surgery.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because movement with tongue protrusion is more suggestive of a lesion associated with the tongue or floor of mouth, not a midline dermoid cyst.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because routine immediate antibiotics are not the key management step for a painless, longstanding congenital lump.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a reactive lymph node is usually tender and related to a recent infection, which does not fit this presentation.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because intra-oral excision including the sublingual gland is the usual operation for a plunging ranula, not a midline dermoid cyst.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
